title: next/font
definition: A built-in Next.js system that automatically optimizes web fonts (like Google Fonts or local custom fonts) and entirely removes layout shifts.
simpleExplanation: Historically, you pasted a Google Fonts link into your HTML. The browser loaded your text in a generic ugly font, then downloaded the Google Font, and then violently swapped the fonts, causing the whole page to jitter. `next/font` downloads the font file *at build time* and serves it locally, guaranteeing zero jitter.
realWorldExample: Implementing the 'Inter' or 'Roboto' font globally across your entire Next.js application with 3 lines of code and zero privacy issues (since the browser never talks to Google's servers).

basic: Does `next/font/google` make an HTTP request to Google's servers every time a user visits your site?
intermediate: What is Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), and how does `next/font` prevent it?

answers.question: HTTP request to Google?
answers.answer: No! Next.js downloads the font file to your own server during the `npm run build` step. The user's browser only talks to your server, ensuring extreme speed and perfect privacy.

answers.question: Prevent CLS?
answers.answer: CLS is when the page jumps around while loading. `next/font` uses a CSS property called `size-adjust` to mathematically force the temporary fallback font to be the EXACT same physical dimensions as the final font, making the swap completely invisible.
